title: How to Make Spiralized Eggplant Bolognese for a Gluten‑Free Dinner
meta_description: Learn how to make a delicious gluten-free spiralized eggplant bolognese with a unique twist on the classic pasta dish.
html:
Welcome to our kitchen where we're cooking up a storm with the help of the Vegetable Spiralizer, a handy gadget that turns zucchini and carrots into low-carb noodles, and now we're taking it up a notch with spiralized eggplant bolognese. This gluten-free dinner is a game-changer for those looking for a healthier take on the classic pasta dish. By using the Vegetable Spiralizer to spiralize eggplant into thin strands, we're able to create a meat sauce infused dish that's both satisfying and nutritious.

Choosing the Right Eggplant

For this recipe, you'll want to choose a firm, heavy eggplant with a glossy exterior. Avoid any eggplants with soft spots or bruises, as they'll be too fragile for spiralizing. You can find these types of eggplants at most grocery stores or farmers' markets in the summer months.

Spiralizing the Eggplant

Now it's time to get started with the spiralizing process. Using your Vegetable Spiralizer, carefully cut the eggplant in half lengthwise and spiralize it into thin strands. You can use the handheld or countertop spiralizer, depending on your preference. Be sure to use a gentle touch to avoid applying too much pressure, which can cause the eggplant to break or tear.

Preparing the Meat Sauce

To make the meat sauce, start by cooking the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks. Once the beef is browned, add in the onion, garlic, and bell pepper, cooking until they're softened and fragrant. Then, add in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. Finally, add in the crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, and salt and pepper to taste. Let the sauce simmer for at least 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.

Assembling the Bolognese

Cook the spiralized eggplant in a large pot of boiling, salted water for 3-5 minutes, or until it reaches your desired level of tenderness. Drain the eggplant and add it to the meat sauce, tossing to combine. Serve the bolognese hot, topped with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh basil leaves.

Gluten-Free Options

This spiralized eggplant bolognese recipe is not only gluten-free, but it's also vegan and paleo-friendly. You can easily substitute the ground beef with ground turkey or pork, or omit it altogether for a vegetarian version. Additionally, you can use different types of vegetables such as zucchini or carrots, which are naturally low in carbs and rich in nutrients.

Additional Tips and Variations

For a creamier bolognese, you can add in some heavy cream or half-and-half towards the end of cooking. You can also add in other vegetables such as mushrooms or spinach for added flavor and nutrition. Experiment with different types of cheese, such as mozzarella or ricotta, for a unique twist on the classic dish.

FAQ

Q: Can I use the Vegetable Spiralizer to spiralize other types of vegetables?

A: Yes, the Vegetable Spiralizer can be used to spiralize a variety of vegetables, including zucchini, carrots, beets, and more.

Q: How do I store leftover spiralized eggplant?

A: You can store leftover spiralized eggplant in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Simply reheat it in the microwave or skillet until it reaches your desired level of tenderness.

Q: Can I make this recipe in a slow cooker?

A: Yes, you can make this recipe in a slow cooker. Simply brown the ground beef in a skillet, then transfer it to the slow cooker with the remaining ingredients and cook on low for 6-8 hours.
